title: SSE silence detection and transcript stitching playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customer escalations surfaced multiple Hosted API cases where clients saw: long silent periods mid-SSE stream, followed by either missing final tokens or duplicate partial transcripts. Root cause investigation shows a combination of (1) transient edge connection blips that didn't trigger our current reconnect heuristics, (2) edge proxies dropping keepalive frames during long-generations, and (3) server-side logic that occasionally emitted a finality marker out-of-band (race) causing clients to treat the stream as terminated before a backfill could be applied. This ticket defines a playbook and an implementation plan to: 1) detect midstream silence (server-side telemetry and client-visible event), 2) emit deterministic chunk markers and idempotent stitch keys, 3) provide a safe backfill protocol for late-arriving tokens, and 4) expose telemetry so SRE/support can rapidly diagnose customer reports. The goal is to reduce customer outages of this class to near-zero and provide a clear recovery path when partial outputs are observed. Work will be gated behind a feature flag and validated with a canary on dedicated infra before rolling to hosted.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a long-generation request (>10s) via Hosted SSE API with streaming enabled and verbose debug logging.
Introduce a 2-6 second TCP pause on the client side (simulate network blip) or drop keepalive packets at the edge proxy.
Observe server continues generating; client experiences a silence window then reconnects (or times out).
If finality marker emitted during silence, client sees truncated transcript; otherwise duplicate fragments may appear on reconnection without idempotent markers.
Capture request IDs, sequence numbers, and server logs; reproduce with both small and large token payloads to validate behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits 'silence' telemetry event when no event sent on SSE stream for configurable threshold (default 2s for long-generation flows).
Generated chunks include deterministic stitch_key and monotonic offset (sequence) that clients can use to dedupe or request a backfill.
Backfill protocol: when late tokens arrive after a client reconnects, server can emit a BACKFILL event which includes original stitch_key and finality marker; clients can stitch without duplication.
Integration tests that simulate edge blips and validate no customer-visible token loss or duplication for 99% of simulated cases.
Telemetry dashboards updated with silence rates, backfill ratios, and affected customer counts; runbook updated and linked in ticket.
Canary rollout on 5% of hosted traffic and one Dedicated customer; no degradation in median latency or token throughput beyond 3%.
Support and SRE trained on new telemetry and playbook within one sprint of rollout.
technical_notes: Silence detector: implement a lightweight per-stream timer in the runtime that emits a telemetry event (SSE_SILENCE) after X ms of inactivity. Make threshold configurable by model class and route.
Stitching keys: use a SHA256(base_request_id + model_version + generation_epoch) truncated to 12 bytes as stitch_key to remain compact and collision-resistant.
Sequence numbers: ensure server assigns a monotonic token_offset for each chunk; include both chunk_seq and token_offset to support variable-size chunks.
Backfill semantics: BACKFILL events are idempotent and must include finality=true when stream generation completes; clients should ignore duplicate token ranges based on stitch_key+token_offset.
Feature flag: runtime.feature.sse_stitching enabled default=false for initial testing. Feature flag toggles both telemetry emission and backfill behavior.
Performance: microbenchmark shows ~0.3% CPU and ~0.5% memory overhead for adding stitch metadata per chunk at 2048-token workloads; acceptable for hosted tiers but evaluate Dedicated SLOs.
Risk: increased SSE payload size may affect tails for low-bandwidth clients; plan to compress stitch metadata and keep fields minimal.

Plan B: if backfill introduces edge cases with proxies that aggressively close idle connections, implement server-side short-lived buffered snapshot endpoint (/v1/streams/:id/snapshot) for clients to fetch missing suffixes.
Testing: unit tests for stitch key generation, integration harness that replays recorded network traces (from incident) and e2e test against customer sample dataset.
Related infra work: extend session-checkpointing in edge gateway to preserve last acked token_offset for faster server reconciliation on reconnects.
comments: 2026-02-18 — Asha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem call for CS case #C-2026-337. Attach incident logs and initial hypothesis about edge proxies dropping keepalives.
2026-02-22 — Liam O'Connor: Reproduced locally using tcpkill simulation; confirmed finality marker out-of-band in two traces. Added preliminary PoC for stitch_key generation (GH-PR-7891).
2026-02-28 — Priya Singh (SRE): Added dashboard query for 'SSE_SILENCE' and baseline telemetry for last 30d. Silence events concentrated on two edge clusters in eu-west-1.
2026-03-03 — Design review: Decided to keep stitch_key short and to prefer BACKFILL event over retrofitting existing 'data' events. UX note: clients may see BACKFILL as a new SSE event type.

2026-03-06 — QA: Integration harness added; found a race where BACKFILL with overlapping token ranges could create duplicates if client reassembly logic is naive — documented fix in client SDK playbook.
2026-03-10 — Liam O'Connor: Feature-flagged rollout plan drafted; canary target: hosted routes tagged 'long-generation' and dedicated customer 'acme-media'. PRs: runtime#7891, sdk-js#342, docs#56.
2026-03-10 — Customer success: Notified acme-media of planned canary and rollback plan; they agreed to participate.
